rules.text: Characters begin at 5 in each of six attributes, may spend up to 15 additional points, and cannot exceed 20. The modifier is floor((score - 10) / 2); max HP is 20 + CON × 2.

In the Stone Guardian encounter, each living character queues one action or Skip during planning. Resolve Round processes all queued actions together, then the surviving Guardian makes one scripted attack against the living character with the lowest current HP. A defeated Guardian cannot take that turn. This is a party batch round, not DEX-based initiative ordering.
Attack checks roll a fair d20 and add the acting character’s STR modifier; the Stone Guardian encounter uses defense 12.

The Stone Guardian uses authored defense 12 and flat armor reduction 1. A hit deals the weapon base damage plus the relevant derived modifier and validated bonuses, reduced by flat armor; damage cannot go below zero and HP is clamped at zero.

Critical chance is 10% plus 0.5 percentage points per DEX above 10. A percentile roll determines criticals. Critical attacks still need to meet normal defense; critical damage is max(1, round((weapon damage + modifiers + bonuses) × 1.5 − 70% of flat armor reduction)).
Successful attacks use the equipped weapon’s authored base damage and apply validated ability bonuses. The engine updates enemy health and records the result.

After all queued player actions, the Stone Guardian rolls d20 + 3 against its selected target’s defense and deals d4 damage on a hit. The target is the living party member with the lowest current HP; ties use stable party IDs.
Characters with 0 HP cannot act. Defeated enemies cannot attack, block travel, or be attacked again.

Initiative rolls with DEX-based ordering, movement and reaction limits, opportunity attacks, and status application from ordinary attacks or abilities are not implemented in this MVP. The current automated enemy behavior is scripted for the Stone Guardian encounter only.
Ability checks support advantage and natural 1/20 outcomes. A separate saving-throw system and incapacitation conditions beyond 0 HP are not implemented.

Ability checks roll a fair d20, add the selected attribute modifier and any valid stored bonus, then compare the total against DC 12. Natural 20 succeeds and natural 1 fails; an advantage option is available to deterministic callers.
A successful check may reveal one matching, undiscovered adventure clue. A clue or reward is recorded once.
Class abilities are defined per character, consume their listed use, and apply only their listed effect.
The model never supplies dice results or applies mechanical effects. The engine is authoritative for rolls, damage, health, inventory, objectives, and encounter state.
The game presents the current scene and relevant discovered information. Players can ask NPCs, inspect, search, travel, use items, or ask read-only narrative questions.

During the Stone Guardian encounter, each living character may queue one action or Skip. Queued characters are locked until resolution; unqueued party members can still act. Resolve Round requires every living member to be ready, commits all results together, writes one round recap, and clears the queue for the next round. A previous-round checkpoint is available after party defeat.

The deterministic parser accepts common action phrasing and adventure location aliases, including taking the hidden crescent as a search and continuing farther down connected crypt paths. Queued round resolution currently applies to the Stone Guardian scene; other adventures continue to resolve supported actions immediately.

Travel follows the selected adventure's connected location graph. Ash Flats bridge checks can be bypassed by securing the bridge with one carried rope; failed exposed crossings cause a stated HP or torch cost while still reaching the node.

Search checks are shared per adventure location. After two failures, later retries gain +2; failures do not complete objectives, and already discovered clues are returned without rerolling or duplication.

At round start, existing Fire, Poison, Dazed, and Recovery statuses tick on party members and Fire/Poison tick on the Guardian. Poison and Fire trigger combustion; Fire can spread among living party members in the same scene; Dazed skips the queued action. Status durations decrease during ticking. Ordinary attacks and abilities do not yet apply statuses. Poison halves potion and Recovery healing. Opportunity attacks, spell slots, and ability cooldown tracking are not implemented.
Deterministic fallback narration uses the selected existing adventure and current location. It supplies scene context but does not generate new story content dynamically.
Narration follows validated engine outcomes. NPC statements are recorded separately from evidence; player theories are never promoted to facts automatically.
